author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That a man ought not to reckon himself worthy of consolation, but more worthy of chastisement

notes.text: (1) Romans ix. 23. (2) Job x. 20, 21. (3) Luke xv. 20. (4) Psalm li. 17.

verses.text: O Lord, I am not worthy of Thy consolation, nor of any spiritual visitation; and therefore Thou dealest justly with me, when Thou leavest me poor and desolate.
verses.modernizedText: O Lord, I am not worthy of Your consolation or of any spiritual visitation, and therefore You deal justly with me when You leave me poor and desolate.

verses.text: For if I were able to pour forth tears like the sea, still should I not be worthy of Thy consolation.
verses.modernizedText: For even if I could pour out tears like the sea, I would still not be worthy of Your consolation.

verses.text: Therefore am I nothing worthy save to be scourged and punished, because I have grievously and many a time offended Thee, and in many things have greatly sinned.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore I am worthy of nothing but to be scourged and punished, because I have grievously and many times offended You, and have greatly sinned in many things.

verses.text: Therefore, true account being taken, I am not worthy even of the least of Thy consolations.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, taking true account, I am not worthy even of the least of Your consolations.

verses.text: But Thou, gracious and merciful God, who willest not that Thy works should perish, to show forth the riches of Thy mercy upon the vessels of mercy,(1) vouchsafest even beyond all his own deserving, to comfort Thy servant above the measure of mankind.
verses.modernizedText: But You, gracious and merciful God, who do not will that Your works should perish, to show the riches of Your mercy upon the vessels of mercy,(1) grant comfort to Your servant beyond all his deserving and beyond the measure given to humankind.

verses.text: For Thy consolations are not like unto the discoursings of men.
verses.modernizedText: For Your consolations are not like the discourses of men.

verses.text: What have I done, O Lord, that Thou shouldst bestow any heavenly comfort upon me?
verses.modernizedText: What have I done, O Lord, that You should bestow any heavenly comfort upon me?

verses.text: I remember not that I have done any good, but have been ever prone to sin and slow to amendment.
verses.modernizedText: I do not remember that I have done any good, but have always been prone to sin and slow to amend my life.

verses.text: It is true and I cannot deny it.
verses.modernizedText: It is true, and I cannot deny it.

verses.text: If I should say otherwise, Thou wouldst rise up against me, and there would be none to defend me.
verses.modernizedText: If I should say otherwise, You would rise up against me, and there would be no one to defend me.

verses.text: What have I deserved for my sins but hell and everlasting fire?
verses.modernizedText: What have I deserved for my sins but hell and everlasting fire?

verses.text: In very truth I confess that I am worthy of all scorn and contempt, nor is it fit that I should be remembered among Thy faithful servants.
verses.modernizedText: In truth I confess that I am worthy of all scorn and contempt, nor is it fitting that I should be remembered among Your faithful servants.

verses.text: And although I be unwilling to hear this, nevertheless I will for the Truth’s sake, accuse myself of my sins, that the more readily I may prevail to be accounted worthy of Thy mercy.
verses.modernizedText: And although I am unwilling to hear this, nevertheless for the sake of the Truth I will accuse myself of my sins, so that I may more readily be accounted worthy of Your mercy.

verses.text: What shall I say, guilty that I am and filled with confusion?
verses.modernizedText: What shall I say, guilty as I am and filled with confusion?

verses.text: I have no mouth to utter, unless it be this word alone, “I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned; have mercy upon me, forgive me.”
verses.modernizedText: I have no words to utter except these alone: “I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned; have mercy upon me, forgive me.”

verses.text: Let me alone, that I may take comfort a little before I go whence I shall not return even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death.(2) What dost Thou so much require of a guilty and miserable sinner, as that he be contrite, and humble himself for his sins?
verses.modernizedText: Leave me alone, that I may take comfort a little before I go where I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death.(2) What do You require so much of a guilty and miserable sinner as that he be contrite and humble himself for his sins?

verses.text: In true contrition and humiliation of heart is begotten the hope of pardon, the troubled conscience is reconciled, lost grace is recovered, a man is preserved from the wrath to come, and God and the penitent soul hasten to meet each other with a holy kiss.(3)
verses.modernizedText: In true contrition and humiliation of heart, hope of pardon is born, the troubled conscience is reconciled, lost grace is recovered, a person is preserved from the wrath to come, and God and the penitent soul hasten to meet each other with a holy kiss.(3)

verses.text: The humble contrition of sinners is an acceptable sacrifice unto Thee, O Lord, sending forth a smell sweeter far in Thy sight than the incense.
verses.modernizedText: The humble contrition of sinners is an acceptable sacrifice to You, O Lord, sending forth a fragrance far sweeter in Your sight than incense.

verses.text: This also is that pleasant ointment which Thou wouldst have poured upon Thy sacred feet, for a broken and contrite heart Thou hast never despised.(4) There is the place of refuge from the wrathful countenance of the enemy.
verses.modernizedText: This also is that pleasant ointment which You would have poured upon Your sacred feet, for You have never despised a broken and contrite heart.(4) There is the place of refuge from the wrathful face of the enemy.

verses.text: There is amended and washed away whatsoever evil hath elsewhere been contracted.
verses.modernizedText: There whatever evil has been contracted elsewhere is amended and washed away.
